matter_name: Ellingson Mineral Company — Da Vinci Incident
case_summary: Ellingson Mineral Company suffered an insider cyberattack in October 1995. Eugene Belford, Head of IT Security, planted the Da Vinci virus — a salami-slicing program designed to divert $0.25 per financial transaction to an offshore account. The virus was deployed by co-conspirator Margo Wallace (VP Operations) using credentials provisioned by Belford. The attack ran for 18 hours before detection by Acting CTO Sarah Chen, who contacted the FBI. The Gibson supercomputer was seized by the Secret Service. Total diverted before detection: $1,047.23. Total projected yield if undetected: $25.1M over 18 months.

parties.client: Ellingson Mineral Company (via CEO Hal Benson)

jurisdiction: Federal — Southern District of New York
key_legal_issues: Computer fraud and unauthorized access (18 U.S.C. § 1030)
CEO/officer liability — what Benson knew and when
privilege_rules: Standard federal common law attorney-client privilege. No specific standing orders. Preservation obligations triggered October 17, 1995 upon Secret Service seizure.
key_custodians: Eugene Belford — primary defendant, Head of IT Security
Sarah Chen — Acting CTO, key fact witness
Richard Gill — IT team, fact witness

critical_dates: 1995-10-15: Wallace plants Da Vinci virus (11:42 PM)
1995-10-16: Virus executes (2:00 AM), Chen detects anomaly (8:14 PM)
